summary.headline: Summary of Periodicals Received by Households for Fiscal Year 2023

statements.text: For all households, periodicals-volume was 3,400.0 millions of pieces in FY2023, which increased by 100.0 millions of pieces from the previous year from FY2022 to FY2023, and decreased by 1,000.0 millions of pieces from five years earlier from FY2018 to FY2023.

caveats: Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology (Appendix A8 table notes). Values before 2010 use the earlier weighting.

Beginning in 2012 data was restated due to weighing by Home Ownership (FY2014 Appendix A, p. 249). Its Table E.2 raised 2012 and 2013 (2012 total: 131.7 billion in FY2012, 130.4 in FY2013, 136.9 in FY2014; packages 3.3 to 3.9; periodicals 5.1 to 5.9), and its notes newly exclude pieces counted as both sent and received. Later reports agree with FY2014, so values from 2012 on share one basis; values through 2011 are on the old one.

From the FY2024 report, results are published as pieces per household per year, and the survey contractor changed (NuStats to RCF). The FY2024 report restated 2014-2023 on its own basis, so its values for those years can differ slightly from earlier reports (e.g. bills paid by mail in 2014: 34% in FY2023, 33% in FY2024).

FY2025 used a new survey design (renamed the Household Mail Survey); Q1 was still covered by the old survey. Age bands changed to Under 45 / 45-64 / 65+ (previously 18-34 / 35-54 / 55+), and 'Large MSA' was redefined in January 2025 from the top 30 metros to metros of 1 million or more.

summary.headline: A comparative long-term summary of Periodicals received by households shows the metric across historical changes, recent intervals, and projections.

statements.text: For All households, periodicals-volume fell by 50.0 percent from 2003 to 2023, crossing the FY2010 and FY2012 methodology breaks.
For All households, periodicals-volume decreased by 42.4 percent since the latest break from 2012 to 2023.
For All households, periodicals-volume decreased by 40.4 percent from 2013 to 2023.
For All households, periodicals-volume fell by 22.7 percent from 2018 to 2023.
For All households, periodicals-volume increased by 3.0 percent from 2022 to 2023.
For All households, the projected periodicals-volume is 2,995.0 million in 2024 with an 80% prediction interval 2,782.0 to 3,209.0.
For All households, the projected periodicals-volume is 2,023.0 million in 2028 with an 80% prediction interval 1,546.0 to 2,500.0.
